text:
Anna (Support): heads-up — ACME (customer) opened a high-severity about embeddings mismatch across our deploys. They say identical text -> hosted returns 1536-d vectors but their Dedicated pool returns 1537. Started after they changed billing/plan and moved some requests through a dedicated endpoint. Request ids: req_h: h12345, req_d: d67890.

Mike (Infra): can you paste the exact curl they used and the model name + any headers? is there a service account JWT involved?

Anna (Support): pasted from customer: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"open-embed-xlarge-v1","input":["Optimize for production economics"]}'` — they claim same token used for both hosted and dedicated paths but creds/channels differ. They also included dedicated endpoint: `https://dedicated-us1.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings` with same payload.

Lee (ML Eng): odd. model open-embed-xlarge-v1 should be 1536 dims. 1537 sounds like an off-by-one memory corruption or extra sentinel float appended. any binary/transport encoding differences? which SDK/version?

Anna (Support): customer SDK is python 2.6.1 (internal name). They say when they batch 8 inputs in a single request to dedicated, they sometimes get one vector with len=1537, rest 1536. On hosted it's stable 1536. They attached a small log: `embedding_len: [1536,1536,1537,1536,1536,1536,1536,1536]`

Mike (Infra): tagging ops-bot to pull traces for req_h and req_d. ops-bot, can you fetch the trace spans and node IDs for h12345 and d67890?

ops-bot: fetching traces... found spans: h12345 -> hosted-node-12 -> model-serving-3; d67890 -> dedicated-node-7 -> model-serving-5. No immediate 5xx. Avg token-time: hosted 18ms/token, dedicated 12ms/token.

Lee (ML Eng): timeline hypothesis: dedicated runtime has an optimization path for batching where KV cache/IO buffer re-use might not zero-pad trailing floats on a small codepath. That could leak an extra float into the final ndarray shape when marshaling to JSON. Hosted runtime compiles a slightly different kernel.

Sara (Product): customer also mentioned this coincided with them changing subscription on the billing dashboard — billing-bot ping?

billing-bot: Billing event: ACME plan upgraded from "team" -> "enterprise-dedicated" at 2027-02-28T15:02:11Z. No quota throttles applied.

Anna (Support): customer mentions toggling between tokens (user vs service) changed behavior: user token -> hosted -> 1536, service token -> dedicated -> occasional 1537. Could token map to a different model variant?

Lee (ML Eng): model variant mapping could do A/B routing, but variants are pinned by model id unless we have a compatibility alias. check model catalog mapping for that customer. Also need random seed — but dimension mismatch isn't about RNG.

Mike (Infra): reproduced locally: I ran a 8-item batch against dedicated staging using their SDK v2.6.1 and toggled batching flags. With continuous batching enabled and batch-size threshold 8, one of the responses sometimes came back with length 1537. Stack trace points to marshalling code path `serialize_embeddings()` in runtime_bin. I can attach snippet:```serialize_embeddings(batch_responses):
  out = []
  for r in batch_responses:
    vec = r.as_float32_list()
    # old path: avoid copy by slicing view
    out.append(vec.view())
  return json.dumps(out)``` 

Mike (Infra): looks like view() used on a pooled buffer. buffer size allocated = num_tokens * dim + pad. For a particular batch, pad not zeroed and view includes one extra float.

Lee (ML Eng): that's consistent. The hosted runtime likely copies into a fresh buffer, cleaning padding, while dedicated uses pooled zeroed buffer only sometimes. Hypothesis: pooled buffer reuse + missing explicit resize/copy -> leaking extra float. root cause in runtime marshalling after quantization/packing.

Anna (Support): next steps — can we provide a short repro for customer and a mitigation for them to use? They want a workaround ASAP.

Mike (Infra): mitigation: set request header `X-Force-Copy: 1` or disable continuous batching by adding query `?batching=false` to dedicated endpoint. Both force copies. Temporary fix we can document. I'll prepare a hotfix patch to runtime to ensure explicit resize/copy on marshalling.

Lee (ML Eng): also add assertion server-side: check reported dim == model.dim and raise 500 with diagnostic if mismatch. That prevents wrong-length vectors from being returned to customers. I'll open PR to add check and also a unit test that simulates pooled buffer with trailing nonzero pad.

Anna (Support): customer needs repro steps to confirm on their side. Proposed message: 1) Try dedicated request with `?batching=false` and compare vector lengths; 2) If using SDK, upgrade to the upcoming v2.6.2 patch (we'll provide) or set header `X-Force-Copy: 1`. 3) Share successful/failed request ids so we can fetch traces. OK?

Sara (Product): agree. let's also offer to roll back them to hosted routing temporarily until patch lands, if they prefer. Offer credit for the disruption.

Anna (Support): I've sent that guidance to ACME and asked for repro request ids. They replied with two example ids and confirmed `?batching=false` made the problem disappear. They want ETA for patch.

Mike (Infra): ETA: hotfix to marshalling pipeline can be staged within 48 hours, full rollout across Dedicated clusters 3-4 days (can canary on a few nodes immediately). I'll start branch `fix/marshall-copy-1801`.

Lee (ML Eng): I'll produce the unit test and add server-side dimension assertion by EOD.

Anna (Support): I'll keep customer updated and propose hosted fallback or disable batching.

Mike (Infra): action items:
- Mike: push hotfix branch + canary config (48h)
- Lee: unit test + assertion (EOD)
- Sara: coordinate rollback/credits with customer success if needed
- Anna: collect repro request ids and confirm customer on workaround

Anna (Support): closing note: this was not an auth token issue after all; billing event coincided with routing -> flows went through dedicated optimized path, which exposed a marshalling bug. Filing internal incident and linking to ticket INC-2027-553. I'll update thread with final PR and release notes when available. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: incident created INC-2027-553, assigned to infra+ml.

Mike (Infra): will update once canary shows no regressions.

Anna (Support): thanks everyone, marking as customer-updated for now.
